ۗ﴿Have you not seen how﴾ means: have you not known. "How" stands in the accusative position, governed by the verb "your Lord did," not by "have you not seen." The clause is the object of "have you not seen." ﴿in misguidance﴾ means: in nullification and ruin. ﴿Ababil﴾ means: groups, one after another. Al-Zamakhshari said: its singular is "ababilah." But the majority of scholars said it is a plural with no singular from its own form. ﴿with stones﴾: It is narrated that each stone was larger than a lentil and smaller than a chickpea. Ibn 'Abbas said: he (Abu Hurayrah? no) — it was reported that he saw near Umm Hani about two baskets of these stones, and that they were streaked with red. It is also narrated that on each stone was the name of the one it would strike, written upon it. ﴿of sijjil﴾: this has already been mentioned. ﴿like eaten husks﴾: "al-'asf" is the leaf and stalk of the crop, and the meaning is that they became crushed and decayed. In likening them to it there are three aspects. The first: He likened them to straw when beasts have eaten it and then dunged it, combining destruction and baseness; but Allah alluded to this in accordance with the courtesy of the Qur'an. The second: he meant the leaves of the crop when worms eat them. The third: he meant a crop whose produce has been eaten while only its husk remains, of no worth.
